title: Cantucci
intro: Tuscan almond biscotti, baked twice for that proper crunch.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and orange zest, then add the 2 eggs and knead.
Work in the almonds with floured hands until evenly spread: the dough stays a little sticky.
Shape 3 logs 3 cm wide, well spaced on the tray, and brush them with the beaten yolk.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the logs are golden and firm to the touch.
steps.label: First bake

steps.t: Let them cool a little, then slice on the diagonal 1.5 cm thick with a serrated knife.
steps.label: Cool slightly

steps.t: Lay the slices cut side down and toast them at 160 °C until dry.
steps.label: Second bake

steps.t: Cool them on a wire rack: they crisp up as they cool.

tips.t: Serve them after dinner with Vin Santo for dunking.
In a tin they stay crisp for a month.

title: Chocolate chip cookies
intro: Crisp edges, a chewy middle and plenty of chocolate: the American classic.

steps.t: Melt the butter and let it cool for a few minutes.
Whisk the butter with both sugars, then add egg and vanilla and mix until glossy.
Add flour, baking soda and salt, then the chocolate chips, mixing only until no flour shows.
Cover and chill the dough: the cookies spread less and stay thick.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll 16 balls and space them well apart on two lined trays.
Bake one tray at a time until the edges are golden and the centre still looks underdone.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 160 °C for 8 minutes, 4 at a time on baking paper, until the edges are golden.

steps.t: Leave them on the tray until set, then move them to a wire rack.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Brown the butter in a pan until it smells nutty: the cookies taste of caramel.
Straight out of the oven, top each one with a few flakes of sea salt.
Raw dough balls freeze well: bake them from frozen for 2 extra minutes.

title: Baci di dama
intro: Two little hazelnut-butter domes joined by a thin layer of dark chocolate.

steps.t: Pulse the hazelnuts with the sugar until they form a fine meal.
Knead the hazelnut meal with butter, flour and salt into a smooth dough.
Wrap the dough in cling film and chill it so it holds its shape.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160 °C. Roll 7 g balls and set them on a lined baking tray.
Bake until the bases are just golden: the balls should keep their dome shape.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool completely on the tray: warm, they break.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Melt the chocolate over simmering water and let it cool until it thickens slightly.
Put a dot of chocolate on the flat side of one biscuit, press another onto it and let it set.

tips.t: Use blanched almonds instead of hazelnuts for the original version from Tortona.
Weigh the balls: if they are all equal, the two halves match perfectly.

title: Jam-filled shortcrust cookies
intro: Two buttery shortcrust rounds with a jam centre peeking through the hole.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll the pastry to 3 mm on a floured surface (if shop-bought, take it out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead).
Cut rounds with a 6 cm cutter, and cut a 2 cm hole in the centre of half of them.
Lay them on a lined baking tray; gather the scraps, roll again and cut more.
Bake until the edges are just golden: they should stay pale.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool completely on the tray.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Dust the rounds with the hole with icing sugar.
Spoon a teaspoon of jam onto each whole round and top with a holed one, pressing lightly.

tips.t: Kids love them even more with raspberry jam or hazelnut spread instead of apricot.
Once filled they soften: if baking ahead, store them unfilled in a tin and fill on the day.

title: Soft amaretti
intro: Almonds, sugar and egg whites: crackled and sugary outside, soft within.

steps.t: In a bowl mix the ground almonds and sugar.
Whisk the whites with the salt to soft peaks and fold them into the almonds with the extract to a firm paste.
Cover and chill the mixture: it firms up and is easier to shape.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Heat the oven to 170 °C. With damp hands roll 20 g balls and coat them in icing sugar.
Set them on a lined tray and press each lightly with two fingers so they crack as they bake.
Bake until the tops are well cracked and the bases just golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool on the tray: warm, they are fragile.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Crumble them over a bowl of vanilla ice cream, or serve them with an espresso.
Add the grated zest of an unwaxed orange or lemon to the mixture.

title: Wine ring biscuits
intro: Rome-area biscuits made with wine and olive oil, no eggs or butter.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
In a bowl stir wine, oil, sugar and salt until the sugar starts to dissolve.
Add flour, baking powder and aniseed a little at a time and knead to a soft dough that doesn't stick.
Pinch off 15 g pieces, roll them into 12 cm ropes and close each into a ring.
Dip one side of each ring in sugar and set them on the trays sugar side up.
Bake until golden underneath and the sugar on top has cracked.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Cool them on a wire rack: they turn crisp.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Dunk them in a glass of red wine, as they do in the taverns south of Rome.
Made with red wine instead of white, they turn darker and more aromatic.
